Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Answers below, with attached redacted artifacts. Ive kept responses short for the SIG; happy to jump on a 30-min sync if you want to run through specifics.

1) Notification timelines (standard):
- Initial advisory: within 24 hours of confirmed detection of an incident that may affect customer data (we may send a high-level advisory sooner if there is immediate operational impact).
- Confirmed impact notice: within 72 hours of confirmation that customer data was accessed or exfiltrated. This is our target window for notifying affected customers with the facts known at that time.
- Remediation/final report: We aim to provide a substantive remediation report within 30 days for incidents requiring customer-level remediation; complex investigations may require longer windows and we communicate expected timelines upfront.

Notes: "Confirmed" means we have validated evidence (logs, KV cache snapshots, or other telemetry) indicating unauthorized access to customer-specific data stores or plaintext customer content. If we need legal or law-enforcement coordination, timelines may shift to accommodate requests.

2) Operational POCs / escalation path (short):
- On-call SRE (incident triage, containment): On-call SRE via PagerDuty (primary contact: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai). For SIG evidence we can provide a redacted on-call roster excerpt.
- Security Lead (investigation, IRT coordination): rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai (Security & Trust lead). Will engage the incident response team and external forensics if needed.
- Legal escalation (customer notification approvals, regulatory counsel): aditya_rao@redwood.ai (Head of Legal Ops) — aditya handles approvals for customer-facing language and escalation to CRO/GC.

After-hours: PagerDuty -> escalation to SRE -> Security Lead -> Legal. We'll provide a redacted escalation matrix in the attachments.

3) Artifacts attached (redacted):
- redwood_sig_responses_20261127.pdf (completed SIG answers, IR section redacted where needed)
- ir_runbook_excerpt_20261127.txt (excerpt: triage checklist, evidence preservation steps, log-hold guidance)

A few additional points we included in the SIG answers:
- We maintain forensic-quality logs for 90 days by default, and extended retention options are configurable on Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Our runbook includes steps for preservation of KV cache snapshots and WASM-based inference artifacts that are commonly asked about in SIG reviews.

If that looks good, let me know and I'll add an explicit CSV escalation matrix and a short example notification timeline template you can use in the SIG.

Regards,

Rishi Malhotra

Redwood Inference

Template (customer-facing) — short:
"On [date], Redwood Inference detected and confirmed unauthorized access to a subset of customer-managed resources. Upon confirmation, we immediately initiated containment and an investigation, engaged our incident response team, and are working with third-party forensics to determine scope. We will notify affected customers directly with the specific accounts impacted, the nature of the data involved, and recommended remediation steps. Initial notifications will be provided within 72 hours of confirmed impact. We are also engaging relevant regulators as required by law."

Clarifications on content of the 72-hour notice:
- We will provide a summary of indicators of compromise, affected customer identifiers (masked/redacted as appropriate), suspected vector if known, immediate mitigations applied, and recommended customer actions.
- If we are unable to provide full details within 72 hours due to ongoing evidence collection or legal restrictions, we will provide an interim advisory with the status and next expected update.
